scenarios.title: Email only, no password
scenarios.description:
A connection configured with a single identifier, email, required, and no password collection. The 
user provides an email address, proves ownership with an email OTP, and completes the signup. This 
is the simplest signup Embedded Authorize supports.
scenarios.alternatePaths:
_Removing a claimed identifier is still under discussion and will be documented as an alternate path separately._

---

happyPaths.label: Happy path 1: required only
happyPaths.title: required only
happyPaths.intro:
The only path for this scenario. Email is the sole required identifier, there are no optional 
steps, and no password is collected.
stepLabels: Start the signup, receiving the identifier menu.
Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

exchanges.note: The client invokes the signup action returned by the initiate call. The server responds with the claim menu of allowed identifiers.

scenarios.title: Email only, optional password
scenarios.description:
A connection configured with a single identifier, email, required, and an optional password. The 
user provides an email address and proves ownership with an email OTP. Once the email is verified, 
the user may either enroll a password or skip it. Both are happy paths.

_Removing a claimed identifier is still under discussion and will be documented as an alternate path separately._

happyPaths.label: Happy path 1: skip the optional password
happyPaths.title: skip the optional password
happyPaths.intro:
Email is verified, then the user confirms without enrolling a password. After the email is 
verified, next offers both enroll:password and signup:confirm; this path takes confirm.
stepLabels: Start the signup, receiving the identifier menu.
Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

exchanges.note: The client invokes the signup action returned by the initiate call. The server responds with the claim menu of allowed identifiers.

exchanges.label: Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

password is optional, signup:confirm remains available throughout; enrolling the password is never

scenarios.title: Email required, phone optional, no password
scenarios.description:
A connection with two identifiers: email (required) and phone (optional), and no password 
collection. The user must collect and verify the email. The phone may be added and verified, or 
skipped entirely. Because the phone is optional, the two happy paths differ by whether the phone is 
included.

Recall the state machine (see signup-state-machine.md): the user may claim both identifiers up 
front while in the wide claim mode, but only one challenge is in flight at a time. signup:confirm
appears only once every required identifier is verified and no claimed identifier is left 
unverified.
scenarios.alternatePaths:
_Removing a claimed identifier is still under discussion and will be documented as an alternate path separately._

---

happyPaths.label: Happy path 1: required only (skip the optional phone)
happyPaths.title: required only (skip the optional phone)
happyPaths.intro:
The user claims and verifies the email, skips the phone, and confirms. The phone offer remains in
next throughout but is never taken.
stepLabels: Start the signup, receiving the identifier menu.
Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

exchanges.label: Start the signup, receiving the identifier menu.
exchanges.note: The client invokes the signup action returned by the initiate call. The server responds with the claim menu of allowed identifiers.

exchanges.label: Provide the email address.
exchanges.note:
The email is claimed. next now offers the email challenge, still offers the optional phone, and 
offers removing the claimed email.

exchanges.label: Send the email OTP.
exchanges.note:
Calling challenge enters the exclusive lane. next narrows to verify plus resend for this 
identifier only.

exchanges.label: Verify the OTP.
exchanges.note:
The email (the only required identifier) is verified. No claimed identifier is left unverified, so
signup:confirm appears. The optional phone is still offered.

exchanges.label: Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

happyPaths.label: Happy path 2: required plus the optional phone
happyPaths.title: required plus the optional phone
happyPaths.intro:
The user claims and verifies the email, then also claims and verifies the phone, then confirms. 
At that branch point the user chooses to add the phone. 
Note that once the phone is claimed but not yet verified, signup:confirm is withheld again (a 
claimed identifier must be verified before confirming).
stepLabels: Start the signup, receiving the identifier menu.
Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

exchanges.label: Start the signup, receiving the identifier menu.
exchanges.note: The client invokes the signup action returned by the initiate call. The server responds with the claim menu of allowed identifiers.

exchanges.label: Provide the email address.
exchanges.note:
The email is claimed. next now offers the email challenge, still offers the optional phone, and 
offers removing the claimed email.

exchanges.label: Send the email OTP.
exchanges.note:
Calling challenge enters the exclusive lane. next narrows to verify plus resend for this 
identifier only.

exchanges.label: Verify the OTP.
exchanges.note:
The email (the only required identifier) is verified. No claimed identifier is left unverified, so
signup:confirm appears. The optional phone is still offered.

exchanges.label: Provide the phone number.
exchanges.note: The phone is claimed. signup:confirm disappears because the phone is now claimed but unverified.

exchanges.label: Verify the OTP.
exchanges.note:
The phone is verified. Now both identifiers are verified and nothing is left unverified, so
signup:confirm appears (the phone offer is gone, as it is now claimed and verified).

exchanges.label: Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

scenarios.title: Email required, phone optional, optional password
scenarios.description:
A connection with email (required), phone (optional), and an optional password. This scenario has 
two optional dimensions, the phone and the password, so the happy paths range from the minimum 
(email only) to the most complete (email, phone, and password). All are happy paths because every 
optional step is a must-have capability.

_Removing a claimed identifier is still under discussion and will be documented as an alternate path separately._

happyPaths.label: Happy path 1: required only (skip phone, skip password)
happyPaths.title: required only (skip phone, skip password)
happyPaths.intro:
The user claims and verifies the email, then confirms. After the email is verified, next offers 
the optional phone, the optional password, and confirm; this path takes confirm directly.

exchanges.label: Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

happyPaths.label: Happy path 2: required plus the optional password (skip phone)
happyPaths.title: required plus the optional password (skip phone)
happyPaths.intro:
The email is collected and verified, then the user enrolls the password and confirms, skipping the 
phone. Note that enrolling the password advances past identifier collection, so the optional phone is 
no longer offered.
stepLabels: Start the signup, receiving the identifier menu.
Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

exchanges.note: The client invokes the signup action returned by the initiate call. The server responds with the claim menu of allowed identifiers.

exchanges.label: Verify the OTP.
exchanges.note: Email verified. next now offers the optional phone, the optional password, and confirm.

exchanges.label: Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

happyPaths.label: Happy path 3: required plus phone plus password (most complete)
happyPaths.title: required plus phone plus password (most complete)
happyPaths.intro:
The user then adds and verifies the phone, then enrolls 
the password, then confirms. The optional phone must be collected before enrolling the password, 
because enrolling the password advances past identifier collection and the phone could no longer be 
added.
stepLabels: Start the signup, receiving the identifier menu.
Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

exchanges.label: Start the signup, receiving the identifier menu.
exchanges.note: The client invokes the signup action returned by the initiate call. The server responds with the claim menu of allowed identifiers.

exchanges.label: Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

scenarios.title: Email required, phone optional, required password

A connection with email (required), phone (optional), and a required password. The email must be 
verified and the password must be enrolled. The phone is the only optional dimension, so there are 
two happy paths: with and without the phone. Because the password is required, signup:confirm is 
withheld until the password is enrolled.

happyPaths.title: required only (skip the optional phone)
happyPaths.intro:

Note that after the email is verified, next offers the optional phone and the required password 
but not confirm; confirm appears only after the password is enrolled.

exchanges.label: Enroll the password.

exchanges.label: Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

happyPaths.label: Happy path 2: required plus the optional phone
happyPaths.title: required plus the optional phone
happyPaths.intro:
Because enrolling the password advances 
past identifier collection, the optional phone must be collected and verified first, then the 
required password is enrolled, then confirm. At Step 5 the user chooses to add the phone rather than 
go straight to the password.
stepLabels: Start the signup, receiving the identifier menu.
Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

exchanges.label: Start the signup, receiving the identifier menu.
exchanges.note: The client invokes the signup action returned by the initiate call. The server responds with the claim menu of allowed identifiers.

exchanges.label: Verify the OTP.
exchanges.note:
Email verified. Because the password is required, next offers the optional phone and the required

exchanges.label: Provide the phone number.
exchanges.note:
Collecting the phone keeps the flow in identifier collection. The password is still offered (it is

exchanges.label: Verify the OTP.
exchanges.note:
Phone verified. Both identifiers are now verified. Because the password is required, next offers

exchanges.label: Confirm the signup, receiving the authorization code.

scenarios.title: Email required, phone required, required password
scenarios.description:
The most complete mandatory configuration: two required identifiers (email and phone) and a 
required password. All three must be satisfied. signup:confirm is withheld until both identifiers 
are verified and the password is enrolled. There is a single happy path.
scenarios.alternatePaths: _Removing a claimed identifier is still under discussion and will be documented as an alternate path separately._
